notes.rule: an operation or mode is DEFINED on scene-referred data when its formula has no reference to the unit white point: no constant 1 or 0.5 grey/threshold, no table or range on [0,1], no clip of its result. Exposure: Adobe documents it for HDR/32-bit, computed at gamma 1 (only linearize_gamma 1 admitted; the 2.2 power stand-in is undefined for negatives). Unsharp: o + amount (o - blur), its threshold gates on an absolute difference (Studio reading). Content-aware: synthesis and the 'none' blend are weighted averages / linear; the colour adaptations clamp adjusted samples to [0, alpha] and bound bias in unit-scale units
notes.research: Foundry Nuke 17.1v2 Merge operations (learn.foundry.com/nuke/content/comp_environment/merging/merge_operations.html, fetched 2026-10-15): screen 'A or B <=1? A+B-AB: max(A,B)', exclusion 'A+B-2AB', divide 'A/B, 0 if A<0 and B<0' (source over backdrop: differs from pigment's backdrop/source -> refused), soft-light 'B(2A+(B(1-AB))) if AB<1, 2AB otherwise' (differs from W3C on [0,1] -> refused), overlay/hard-light/colour-dodge/burn given as prose only -> refused. The unversioned Nuke reference-guide Screen page states the condition as '0<A<1 and 0<B<1': UNVERIFIED which matches Nuke's runtime (D5). Adobe's blending-modes help page (helpx.adobe.com) returned HTTP 403; a search summary lists Normal, Dissolve, Darken, Multiply, Lighten, Linear Dodge, Difference, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity as 32-bit modes, but no formula: Photoshop 32-bit parity UNVERIFIED (D5)
